cards.text: This letter goes to believers who've been through a lot, and the writer just told them, 'You need to persevere.' He says we aren't the kind who shrink back, we're the kind who have faith. So now he stops to say what faith actually IS.

cards.question: Faith, the writer says, is the assurance of what we hope for. True or false: He says faith is also the certainty of what we can already see.

cards.text: This, he says, is why the ancients were commended. Faith got them into the Hall of Fame, and this man is about to call out the names like a stadium announcer on game night.

cards.question: Before any names, the writer goes all the way back. By faith we understand the universe was formed at God's command. So what does he say everything we see was made out of?

cards.text: First name up: Abel, son of Adam and Eve (Genesis 4:1-2). By faith he offers God a better sacrifice than his brother Cain did.

cards.question: Abel's sacrifice was better, and God gave approval to his gifts. By faith, what was Abel commended as?
True or false: The writer says that even though Abel is dead, by faith he still speaks.

cards.text: Abel died way back at the start of the Bible, and the man is STILL talking. Me? I was alive the whole time in that junk drawer and could barely get out a 'good morning.'
Next: Enoch, Noah's great-grandfather (Genesis 5:21-29). By faith he was taken up so that he did not see death: "He could not be found, because God had taken him away."
I bet folks looked high and low for him, the way I hunt for my rolling pin every single morning. And that man was just GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Before Enoch was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.
Then the writer says without faith it's impossible to please God. Anyone who approaches Him must believe that He ___ and that He ___ those who earnestly seek Him.

cards.text: Then comes Noah. He gets warned about things not yet seen, and he responds in godly fear.
Picture an alert on your phone about something nobody has EVER seen. Most of us hit snooze, but not Noah.

cards.question: Noah's been warned about things not yet seen. In godly fear, what does he build?

answers.text: An ark to save his family
A tower to reach the sky

cards.question: By building that ark, Noah ___ the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

cards.text: Next name: Abraham, the man God promised to make into a great nation (Genesis 12:1-2). By faith, when he's called to go to a place he'd later receive as his inheritance, he obeys.

cards.question: True or false: Abraham obeyed and went, even though he didn't know where he was going.

cards.text: No map, no directions, just GO. Friend, I live on a planet barely big enough for one bakery and I STILL double check which way the oven is.
By faith he dwells in the promised land, but as a stranger in a foreign country.

cards.question: Abraham is in the promised land, living there as a stranger. What does he live in?

cards.text: Isaac and Jacob, his son and grandson (Genesis 21:3; 25:26), live in tents too, heirs with him of the same promise. Three generations in tents, friend, that's not camping anymore, that's a family tradition.

cards.question: Abraham's in a tent, but he's looking forward to something sturdier: the city with ___, whose architect and builder is God.

cards.text: Now Sarah, Abraham's wife (Genesis 17:15). She's barren and beyond the proper age, but by faith she's enabled to conceive a child.

cards.question: Sarah was past the age, and by faith she was enabled to conceive. What does the writer say was behind it?

answers.text: She considered God faithful to His promise
She asked a prophet to pray for her
She waited for a sign from heaven

cards.text: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, come descendants. Abraham makes the Hall of Fame and THAT'S the line they put on his plaque.

cards.question: From that one man who was as good as dead, how many descendants come?

answers.text: As many as the stars and the sand
Enough to fill one small town
Just one family of twelve sons

cards.text: Then the writer looks at all of them together. All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised.

cards.question: True or false: Even though they never received the promised things, these people saw them and welcomed them from afar.
They acknowledged they were strangers and exiles on the earth. The writer says people who talk like that are seeking what?

answers.text: A way back to their old home
A king to rule over them

cards.text: If they'd been thinking of the country they left, they would have had the chance to go back. Me? Offer me my old spot in the junk drawer and I'm saying NO THANK YOU before you finish the sentence.

cards.question: Instead of the country they left, they were longing for a better country, a ___ one.
True or false: Because they longed for that better country, God is ashamed to be called their God.

cards.text: God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them. And friend, the writer is NOT done calling names, so stick around.

findings.problem: The single-quoted line 'You need to persevere.' is presented as the writer's words, but the BSB has a comma, not a period: "You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God..." (Hebrews 10:36). Either match the BSB wording and punctuation exactly or paraphrase it without quotation marks.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says 'By building that ark, Noah ___ the world,' but the BSB says 'By faith he condemned the world' (Hebrews 11:7). The card claims a link between the ark and condemning the world that the BSB text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke 'THAT'S the line they put on his plaque' makes fun of Abraham being 'as good as dead,' which is a joke about his age. It laughs at Abraham instead of with his situation.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: The right answer 'As many as the stars and the sand' sounds like the Bible, while 'Enough to fill one small town' sounds modern and casual. The right answer stands out by tone alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
